ops.title: spawnllm Go binding verified by execution: pure Go, but three design assumptions were wrong
ops.body:
Verified 2026-07-26 by running code, not reading docs. Probes under `/tmp/ccn-exec/spawnllm/{probe,coreprobe}`. Module: `github.com/yasyf/spawnllm/go@v0.10.0` (tag `go/v0.10.0`); checkout at `~/Code/spawnllm` is `v0.10.0-21-g2255dfb`, source-identical to the release.

**The critical answer is a clean pass: no cgo.** The core is a `//go:embed spawnllm_core.wasm` blob (371,813 bytes) run under wazero with `wasi_snapshot_preview1`. `CGO_ENABLED=0` builds and vets clean and cross-compiles to linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64. Third-party closure is wazero, `invopop/jsonschema` (+ `bahlo/generic-list-go`, `buger/jsonparser`, `pb33f/ordered-map/v2`, `go.yaml.in/yaml/v4`) and `golang.org/x/sys`. `go.mod` requires go 1.26, matching cc-notes' floor.

**One real cost: +6.2 MB stripped** (7.36 MB vs a 1.16 MB empty-main baseline), split between wazero and the embedded blob, landing on every cross-compiled release binary. Argues for keeping spawnllm in the daemon binary rather than the base `cc-notes` CLI.

**Also note: the local checkout alone cannot compile** — the wasm blob is gitignored and ships only on release tags, so a `replace` onto `~/Code/spawnllm` fails. Consume the tagged module from the proxy.

## Three assumptions that were wrong

**`map_concurrent` does not exist in Go — REFUTED.** It is Python-only; the Go module has zero concurrency helpers. The daemon owns its own fan-out (`errgroup.Group` with `SetLimit(n)` over `RunOn`), which works and is genuinely parallel, but the concurrency limit becomes ours to choose and defend.

**`openai_endpoint` IS reachable from Go — REFUTED, and this opens a door.** `spawnllm.OpenAIEndpoint(baseURL, model, OpenAIOpts{APIKey, Client})` is exported, compiles, and works today against Ollama / llama.cpp / LM Studio on localhost. It is the **only in-process lane** — `httpbackend.go` issues the request with `net/http`, no subprocess — and because the `*http.Client` is injectable it is the only lane fake-able with an `httptest.Server` and no real provider. It must be selected explicitly (absent from the core's auto-selection priority) and model tiers do not apply. `mlx` by contrast is confirmed unreachable: the core rejects the provider variant outright.

**"Direct Go binding ⇒ no subprocess" — CORRECTION.** Every claude / codex / gemini / antigravity call is still `exec.Command` against the provider CLI, with temp files, an isolated config dir and a 180 s per-attempt timeout. What the Go module removes is the *Python* CLI and runtime — one process layer, not two. Process supervision, zombie reaping and the `SIGTERM` + 2 s `WaitDelay` shutdown path remain the daemon's problem.

## Confirmed as asserted

Three bindings off one Rust/WASM core; `small` → haiku / `gpt-5.4-mini:low` / `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` (plus antigravity → `gemini-3.5-flash`); retry defaults to `MaxAttempts` 5 with a 5/15/45 s transient-only ladder; `APIAuth` zero value is `false` so the planner emits `env_unset` and calls bill the subscription.

Structured output is confirmed for Python and **caveated for Go**: `Extract[T]` is strictified but `RunSpec.Schema` is passed to the provider verbatim, no strictifier is exported, and the raw path never populates `Result.Parsed`.

## Latency is the headline for an enrichment lane

Live, subscription-billed, small models: claude `haiku` **38.6 s** for a one-word reply, **87.3 s** with a schema; codex `gpt-5.4-mini:low` **4.5 s** — roughly **9× faster**. Four concurrent claude calls: 57 s wall. The cost is CLI startup plus a subscription round trip, not model time. **Route enrichment to codex.** spawnllm's own specialty routing prefers claude for `general`, which is the slow one; `debugging`/`review` already prefer codex.

## A live blocker on this machine

Isolated claude runs cannot authenticate. `UseHostConfig: false` (the default) makes the core seed an isolated config dir from `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, falling back to keychain item `Claude Code-credentials-<sha256(config_home)[:8]>`. Measured here: the credentials file does not exist, and the keychain holds the **unsuffixed** `Claude Code-credentials` while the core correctly computes and then fails to find `Claude Code-credentials-c25ff9d8`. Every isolated claude run dies with `Not logged in · Please run /login`, while the host CLI works fine.

`CallOpts` has **no `UseHostConfig` field**, so `Call` and `Extract` cannot escape it — which makes `Extract[T]`, the only path that populates `Result.Parsed` and the only path that resolves a `ModelTier`, unusable against claude here. The daemon's claude lane must go through `RunOn` + `UseHostConfig: true`: literal model ids, parse `Result.Raw` yourself, and accept that claude then runs against the real `~/.claude`. A launchd-run daemon will additionally need keychain ACL access even once the naming is reconciled. Worth an upstream spawnllm issue.
